spots.name: St. Michael's Cave
spots.summary: St. Michael's Cave or Old St. Michael's Cave is a network of limestone caves located within the Upper Rock Nature Reserve in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar, at a height of over 300 metres (980 ft) above sea level.

names.ja: サン・マイケル洞窟

spots.name: Cathedral of St. Mary the Crowned

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of Saint Mary the Crowned is a Latin Catholic cathedral in Gibraltar. It is the primary centre of Catholic worship in the Diocese of Gibraltar.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of St. Mary the Crowned

names.es: Catedral de Santa María la Coronada
names.ja: セント・マリー・ザ・クラウンズ教会

spots.name: Europa Point Lighthouse
spots.summary: The Europa Point Lighthouse, also referred to as the Trinity Lighthouse at Europa Point and the Victoria Tower or La Farola in Llanito, is a lighthouse at Europa Point, on the southeastern tip of the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar, on the southern end of the Iberian Peninsula, at the entrance to the Mediterranean Sea.

names.ja: エウローパ岬灯台

spots.name: Ibrahim-al-Ibrahim Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ibrahim-al-Ibrahim Mosque, also known as the King Fahd bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Mosque or the Mosque of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, is an Islamic mosque located at Europa Point in the British overseas territory of Gibraltar, a peninsula connected to southern Spain.

names.ja: イブラヒム＝アル＝イブラヒムのモスク
names.zh: 易卜拉欣-易卜拉欣清真寺

spots.name: Moorish Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Moorish Castle is the name given to a medieval fortification in Gibraltar comprising various buildings, gates, and fortified walls, with the dominant features being the Tower of Homage and the Gate House. Part of the castle itself also housed the prison of Gibraltar until it was relocated in 2010.

names.ja: ムーア城

spots.name: Cathedral of the Holy Trinity

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Holy Trinity is the cathedral for the Church of England Diocese of Europe. Located in Cathedral Square, it is sometimes referred to simply as Gibraltar Cathedral, although it should not be confused with the Cathedral of St. Mary the Crowned, which is Gibraltar's Roman Catholic cathedral.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of the Holy Trinity, Gibraltar

names.ja: ホーリー・トリニティ教会

spots.name: Gorham's Cave

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Gorham's Cave is a sea-level cave in the British overseas territory of Gibraltar. Though not a sea cave, it is often mistaken for one.

names.ja: ゴーラム洞窟

spots.name: Main Street
spots.summary: Main Street is the main arterial street in the British overseas territory of Gibraltar.

names.ja: メイン・ストリート

spots.name: John Mackintosh Square
spots.summary: John Mackintosh Square is a main square in the British overseas territory of Gibraltar. It has been the centre of city life since the 14th century and takes its name from John Mackintosh, a local philanthropist. Notable buildings on John Mackintosh Square include the Parliament Building and the City Hall.

names.ja: ジョン・マッキントッシュ・スクエア

spots.name: Gibraltar Nature Reserve
spots.summary: The Gibraltar Nature Reserve is a protected nature reserve in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar that covers over 40% of the territory's land area. It was established as the Upper Rock Nature Reserve in 1993 under the International Union for Conservation of Nature's category Ia and was last extended in 2013.

names.es: Reserva natural del Peñón de Gibraltar
names.ja: アッパー・ロック自然保護区

spots.name: Winston Churchill Avenue
spots.summary: Winston Churchill Avenue is an arterial road in the British overseas territory of Gibraltar, connecting it with Spain. Once the customs are crossed, the avenue becomes the dual carriageway CA-34.

spots.name: Grand Casemates Square
spots.summary: Grand Casemates Square is the larger of the two main squares within the city centre of Gibraltar. The square takes its name from the British-built Grand Casemates, a casemate and bombproof barracks at the northern end of the square completed in 1817.

names.ja: グランド・ケースメーツ・スクエア

spots.name: Gibraltar Museum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Gibraltar National Museum is a national museum of the history, culture and natural history of Gibraltar located within the city centre of the British overseas territory of Gibraltar.

names.ja: ジブラルタル博物館

spots.name: Trafalgar Cemetery
spots.summary: The Trafalgar Cemetery is a cemetery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. Formerly known as the Southport Ditch Cemetery, it occupies a small area of land just to the south of the city walls, in what had been a defensive ditch during the period of Spanish rule of Gibraltar.

names.ja: トラファルガー墓地

spots.name: O'Hara's Battery
spots.summary: O'Hara's Battery is an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is located at the highest point of the Rock of Gibraltar, near the southern end of the Upper Rock Nature Reserve, in close proximity to Lord Airey's Battery.

names.ja: オハラ砲台

spots.name: Great Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Great Synagogue of Gibraltar, also known as Kahal Kadosh Sha'ar HaShamayim, is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located in the British overseas territory of Gibraltar.

names.ja: グレート・シナゴーグ

spots.name: Gibraltar Botanic Gardens
spots.summary: The Gibraltar Botanic Gardens or La Alameda Gardens are a botanical garden in Gibraltar, spanning around 6 hectares. The Rock Hotel lies above the park.

names.ja: アラメダ庭園

spots.name: Napier of Magdala Battery
spots.summary: Napier of Magdala Battery is a former coastal artillery battery on the south-western cliffs of the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar, overlooking the Bay of Gibraltar. It also overlooks Rosia Bay from the north, as does Parson's Lodge Battery from the south. It contains one of two surviving Armstrong 100-ton guns.

names.ja: ネイピア・オブ・マグダラ砲台

spots.name: Sikorski Memorial
spots.summary: The Sikorski Memorial in Gibraltar commemorates the 1943 Gibraltar B-24 crash of 4 July 1943 which caused the death of General Władysław Sikorski, the commander-in-chief of the Polish Army and Prime Minister of the Polish government in exile.

spots.name: Charles V Wall
spots.summary: The Charles V Wall is a 16th-century defensive curtain wall that forms part of the fortifications of the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. Originally called Muralla de San Benito, it was built in 1540 and strengthened in 1552 by Holy Roman Emperor Charles V.

spots.name: Victoria Stadium
spots.summary: Victoria Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Gibraltar. It is currently used mostly for football matches, but also hosts the annual Gibraltar Music Festival. It is located close to Gibraltar Airport just off Winston Churchill Avenue. It was named after the wife of Gibraltarian philanthropist John Mackintosh.

names.ja: ヴィクトリア・スタジアム

spots.name: Spur Battery
spots.summary: Spur Battery is an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is located in the Upper Battery area of the southern end of the Upper Rock Nature Reserve, just southwest of O'Hara's Battery.

spots.name: American War Memorial
spots.summary: The American War Memorial is a World War I memorial in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It was built for the American Battle Monuments Commission in 1933, and incorporated into the main city wall, the Line Wall Curtain.

names.ja: アメリカ戦争記念門

spots.name: Princess Anne's Battery
spots.summary: Princess Anne's Battery is an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is located on Willis's Plateau at the northern end of the Upper Rock Nature Reserve, below Princess Caroline's Battery. It was named after Anne, Princess Royal and Princess of Orange, the eldest daughter of George II.

spots.name: Harding's Battery
spots.summary: Harding's Battery is a restored artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is located at Europa Point and includes the Europa Sunken Magazine that is now used as a visitor centre.

names.ja: ハーディングの砲台

spots.name: Breakneck Battery
spots.summary: Breakneck Battery is an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is located on Ministry of Defence property at the Upper Rock Nature Reserve, north of Lord Airey's Battery.

spots.name: Princess Caroline's Battery
spots.summary: Princess Caroline's Battery is an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is located at the northern end of the Upper Rock Nature Reserve, at the junction of Willis's Road and Queen's Road. The nearby Princess Anne's Battery is often mistakenly referred to as Princess Caroline's Battery.

names.ja: プリンセス・キャロライン砲台

spots.name: O'Hara's Tower
spots.summary: O'Hara's Tower was a watchtower in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It was located at the highest point of the Rock of Gibraltar, at what is now O'Hara's Battery, near the southern end of the Upper Rock Nature Reserve.

spots.name: Devil's Gap Battery
spots.summary: Devil's Gap Battery is a coastal battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar, overlooking the Bay of Gibraltar near the westernmost limits of the Upper Rock Nature Reserve.

spots.name: Grand Casemates Gates
spots.summary: Grand Casemates Gates, formerly Waterport Gate, provide an entrance from the northwest to the old, fortified portion of the city of the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar, at Grand Casemates Square.

spots.name: King's Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The King's Chapel is a small chapel in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is located at the southern end of Main Street and adjoins the Governor of Gibraltar's residence, The Convent. What nowadays is King's Chapel was the first purpose-built church to be constructed in Gibraltar.

names.ja: キングス教会

spots.name: Lord Airey's Battery
spots.summary: Lord Airey's Battery is an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is located near the southern end of the Upper Rock Nature Reserve, just north of O'Hara's Battery. It was named after the Governor of Gibraltar, General Sir Richard Airey. Construction of the battery was completed in 1891.

spots.name: Gibraltar War Memorial
spots.summary: The Gibraltar War Memorial is a First World War monument located on Line Wall Road in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. Also known as the British War Memorial, it was sculpted by Jose Piquet Catoli of Spain and unveiled in 1923.

names.ja: ジブラルタル戦争記念碑

spots.name: Nefusot Yehuda Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Nefusot Yehuda Synagogue, officially the Kahal Kadosh Nefusot Yehuda, more commonly known as the Flemish Synagogue, sometimes known as the Line Wall Synagogue, is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 65 Line Wall Road, in Gibraltar, a British overseas territory of the United Kingdom.

spots.name: Abudarham Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Abudarham Synagogue is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 19 Parliament Lane, in Gibraltar, a British overseas territory of the United Kingdom.

spots.name: St Andrew's Church, Gibraltar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Andrew's Church was a congregation of the Church of Scotland in the British overseas territory of Gibraltar and was part of the Presbytery of Europe, until it closed in December 2022.

spots.name: Rock Gun Battery
spots.summary: Rock Gun Battery is an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is located on the North Face of the Rock of Gibraltar at the northern end of the Upper Rock Nature Reserve, above Green's Lodge Battery. The emplacement on Middle Hill is at the northern summit of the Rock.

spots.name: Cathedral Square
spots.summary: Cathedral Square is a square within the city centre of the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is the location of the Church of England Cathedral of the Holy Trinity which stands to the eastern end of the square.

names.ja: カシドラル・スクエア

spots.name: Princess Royal's Battery
spots.summary: Princess Royal's Battery is an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is located on Willis's Plateau at the northern end of the Upper Rock Nature Reserve, just southeast of Princess Anne's Battery.

spots.name: Jews' Gate Cemetery
spots.summary: Jews' Gate Cemetery is a Jewish cemetery located on Windmill Hill within a nature reserve in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. Also known as the Windmill Hill Cemetery, it is the site of the earliest known Jewish burials in Gibraltar. The cemetery opened by 1746 and closed in 1848.

names.es: Cementerio de la Puerta de los Judíos

spots.name: Spy Glass Battery
spots.summary: Spy Glass Battery or Spyglass Battery was originally a high angle artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. The battery is mounted high on the rock to give extra range and protection. The battery was still in use during the Second World War as a listening post and site for a Bofors Gun.

spots.name: Parson's Lodge Battery
spots.summary: Parson's Lodge Battery is a coastal battery and fort in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar.

names.ja: パースンズ・ロッジ砲台

spots.name: Leonora's Caves

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Leonora's Caves is a limestone cave system in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. They are located within Old St. Michael's Cave.

spots.name: Queen's Gate, Gibraltar
spots.summary: Queen's Gate is a city gate in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. A large population of Barbary macaques reside in this area, making it a major tourist attraction. Most of the macaques sleep within an area of 9 hectares around the Queen's Gate.

spots.name: Grand Battery
spots.summary: Grand Battery is an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. To the west of the grand battery was a very formidable flank which was considered to have been a "great annoyance to the besiegers."

spots.name: Alameda Wildlife Conservation Park
spots.summary: The Alameda Wildlife Conservation Park (AWCP) is a small wildlife park situated in the Botanic Gardens in Gibraltar.

names.ja: アラメダ野生生物保護公園

spots.name: Martin's Cave

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Martin's Cave is a cave in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It opens on the eastern cliffs of the Rock of Gibraltar, below its summit at O'Hara's Battery. It is an ancient sea cave, though it is now located over 700 feet (210 m) above the shore of the Mediterranean Sea.

spots.name: Wilson's Cave

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wilson's Cave is a cave in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar.

spots.name: Signal Hill Battery
spots.summary: Signal Hill Battery or Signal Battery was an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. The battery was mounted high on the rock. Little remains today as the Gibraltar Cable Car top station was built on the site of the old battery.

spots.name: Gibraltar Methodist Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Gibraltar Methodist Church is part of the South East District of the Methodist Church of Great Britain. It has a long history associated with the development of British Gibraltar, and it has greatly strengthened its ties with the local population since the scaling down of Britain-based forces in recent years.

spots.name: Green's Lodge Battery
spots.summary: Green's Lodge Battery is an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It is located on the North Face of the Rock of Gibraltar at the northern end of the Upper Rock Nature Reserve, above Farringdon's Battery.

spots.name: Garrison Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Garrison Library was founded in Gibraltar in 1793 by Captain John Drinkwater Bethune.

names.ja: ガリスン図書館

spots.name: Prince Edward's Gate
spots.summary: Prince Edward's Gate is a city gate at the entrance to Prince Edward's Road in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It cuts through Charles V Wall, one of the 16th century fortifications of Gibraltar at the former southern limit of the city.

spots.name: Moorish Wall
spots.summary: The Moorish Wall, also known as the Philip II Wall and formerly the Muralla de San Reymondo, is a defensive curtain wall built in the 16th century that formed part of the southern fortifications of the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It was completed by 1575.

spots.name: Farringdon's Battery
spots.summary: Farringdon's Battery is an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. Named after Sir Anthony Farrington, 1st Baronet, it is located above the north face of the Rock of Gibraltar within the Upper Rock Nature Reserve.

spots.name: The Little Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Little Synagogue, otherwise known as Ets Hayim Synagogue, is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 91 Irish Town, in Gibraltar, a British overseas territory of the United Kingdom. The synagogue was established in 1759.

spots.name: Goat's Hair Twin Caves

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Goat's Hair Twin Caves are in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. The caves are listed in the Heritage and Antiquities Act as they are sites of Palaeolithic and Neolithic archaeology.

spots.name: Prince Ferdinand's Battery
spots.summary: Prince Ferdinand's Battery was an artillery battery in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. Today the area is known as the Apes' Den and is the main location for tourists to see Barbary macaques in Gibraltar.

spots.name: Monkey's Cave

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Monkey's Cave is a cave in the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar. It has been used as part of the Fortifications of Gibraltar and in 1942 there was a convalescent hospital here. This building was later used as the HQ of the Royal Electrical & Mechanical Engineers.

spots.name: Siege Tunnels
spots.summary: A system of tunnels dug during the Great Siege which acted as a defence system.

spots.name: The Lord Nelson
spots.summary: The official home of the Gibraltar Rugby Club and Live Music Venue of the Year, with entertainment on stage every night. Offers free WiFi.
